name: Coaptite pivotal
question: Is urethral calcium hydroxylapatite noninferior to bovine dermal collagen for stress urinary incontinence caused by intrinsic sphincter deficiency in women without urethral hypermobility?

design.population: Women with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency and no associated urethral hypermobility.
design.locator: PubMed abstract, Objectives and Methods; FDA SSED p6

verdictNote: FDA review found noninferiority; the journal abstract reports a nonsignificant superiority comparison.
takeaway: Calcium hydroxylapatite (Coaptite) met the prespecified noninferiority criterion versus bovine dermal collagen (Contigen) for 12-month Stamey-grade improvement in women with intrinsic sphincter deficiency; the published complete-case comparison was 63.4% versus 57.0% (P = 0.34).

reports.label: Pivotal comparative trial
reports.citation: Mayer RD, Dmochowski RR, Appell RA, et al. "Multicenter Prospective Randomized 52-Week Trial of Calcium Hydroxylapatite Versus Bovine Dermal Collagen for Treatment of Stress Urinary Incontinence." *Urology.* 2007;69(5):876-880. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2007.01.050
reports.followUp: 12 months after initial injection; complete-case efficacy data for 231/296 treated women

results.measure: At least one Stamey-grade improvement at 12 months, complete cases
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin was based on 15% of the control response proportion; FDA judged noninferiority met. Published P value tests between-group difference, not noninferiority.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; FDA SSED pp9,12,17, Table 7

results.measure: At least one Stamey-grade improvement at 12 months, treated population with last observation carried forward
results.note: FDA regulatory analysis; differs from the journal abstract's complete-case denominators.

harms.label: Treatment-related urinary retention
harms.note: Percentages reported without patient counts; treated safety populations were 158 and 138.

harms.label: Unanticipated treatment-related serious tissue dissection or erosion
harms.note: FDA review described tissue bridges and erosion in two Coaptite recipients; attribution to device versus technique was uncertain.

delivery.label: Injection protocol
delivery.value: Cystoscopic urethral injection under anesthesia; up to five treatment sessions, with repeat sessions allowed in the first six months.
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods; FDA SSED p9, Treatment

delivery.label: Initial injection route
delivery.note: Periurethral injection was permitted at investigator discretion.

delivery.label: Single-session treatment during study
delivery.locator: PubMed abstract, Results; denominators confirmed in FDA SSED p6
delivery.note: P = 0.034. Counts refer to all treated women, unlike the FDA SSED complete-case treatment table.

delivery.label: Mean total injected volume over study
delivery.note: P < 0.0001; FDA SSED complete-case table reports 6.8 mL for collagen.
